fields.title: Nvidia cuts its fiscal-2028 growth outlook on February 24
fields.text: At its fiscal fourth-quarter report, projected for February 24, 2027, Nvidia lowers its outlook for fiscal-2028 revenue growth below the roughly 75% it gave on November 17, 2026, or withdraws it.
fields.resolution_source: Nvidia fiscal Q4 2027 earnings release and call

chances.note: Nvidia raised this outlook to 75% from 70% a week ago with demand ahead of supply, so a cut within one quarter needs something to change. Three things can: the 90-day licence deadline for overseas data centres serving Chinese customers falls about ten days before the report, on sales Luria puts at 5% to 20% of the total; customer financing ('access to capital for a large number of neoclouds is going to disappear' if Nvidia stops guaranteeing, per Apollo's Rowan), with the $500 billion plan yet to fund a deal; and an interim or newly arrived CEO resetting the bar. One in five.

passages: After NVIDIA’s quarterly report, Luria said demand remained strong enough for the company to raise its fiscal 2028 growth outlook to 75% from 70%, even as it acknowledged uncertainty around Asian sales.

Luria estimates that 5% to 20% of NVIDIA chip sales may have reached China directly or through resellers and Asian data centers, which drove his price-target reduction to \$200 from \$300, despite maintaining a Buy rating.

Data centers that already serve those customers have 90 days to obtain a license. Operators are also expected to check who ultimately owns their clients, and a customer that refuses to answer is treated as a red flag.

On Tuesday’s [Nvidia earnings call](https://www.benzinga.com/content/63374236/nvidia-q3-2027-earnings-call-transcript), Kress said the company would be selective about the deals it backs. Apollo CEO **Marc Rowan** told CNBC that if Nvidia stopped acting as guarantor, "access to capital for a large number of neoclouds is going to disappear." Those companies buy chips and rent out the computing power.

to.title: Nvidia keeps its fiscal-2028 outlook at about 75%
to.text: At its February 24, 2027 report Nvidia reaffirms fiscal-2028 revenue growth of about 75%.
to.resolution_source: Nvidia fiscal Q4 2027 earnings release and call

to.title: Nvidia raises its fiscal-2028 outlook above 75%
to.text: At its February 24, 2027 report Nvidia raises its outlook for fiscal-2028 revenue growth above 75%.
to.resolution_source: Nvidia fiscal Q4 2027 earnings release and call

chances.note: It raised the figure last quarter and guided fourth-quarter revenue to $130 billion against about $125 billion expected, with the Vera Rubin ramp its fastest. A second raise in a row is plausible but less likely than holding while the export and financing questions are open: three in ten.

shock.note: The November beat-and-raise did not lift the shares: they fell 5.2% beyond the factors from Nov 11 to Nov 18 (window) because leadership and export questions dominated. A second raise helps more if those have eased by February; I allow 5% beyond what the shares would otherwise do.
Nvidia is about 22% of TSMC's 2026 sales; a higher Nvidia outlook is a higher order book for TSMC.

The 75% outlook is what holds analysts' targets (Luria cut his to $200 from $300 on the China question alone and kept a Buy). The shares are already down 35% since Oct 1 (window) with ten bank downgrades; a cut would confirm the bear case that sales rested on China-linked buyers and on Nvidia's own financing. 12% beyond what the shares would otherwise do.
TSMC lost 4.2% beyond the factors from Nov 11 to Nov 18 on doubts about Nvidia's orders alone (window); a cut to Nvidia's outlook makes the doubt a fact for its largest customer.

Nvidia is the largest weight in the chip sector and its outlook is the sector's demand signal; memory, equipment and networking names fell 7-8% on Nov 16 on export news about Nvidia's customers. 3% for the sector beyond the market.
